thread:
Samir: Quick FYI — we merged the jemalloc security patch (6.2.1) to address CVE-2025-9999 and pushed to staging at 14:02 UTC. Need post-patch validation checklist and a canary plan before prod rollout.
Maria: Thanks. Any immediate regressions in staging smoke? cpu/mem/allocs?
Jin: ran the basic smoke suite -> app starts, endpoints healthy. Short load run (10m, 200rps) showed +8% resident mem vs baseline but steady. No crashes.
Oliver: +8% resident could be concerning for long-lived services. Did you run the allocation profiling? jemalloc changes can change fragmentation patterns.
Jin: ran jemalloc profiling (jeprof) for 5m, sample attached (summary pasted):
```
heap_live: baseline 1.2GB -> patched 1.3GB
active: baseline 850MB -> patched 920MB
fragmentation est +9%
```
Maria: Ok. Two action items: 1) longer soak (2h) under p95 production-like traffic on a canary host, 2) add observability queries for fragmentation and arena counts.
Samir: Agree. Suggest canary rollout 3 hosts (5% traffic) for 2 hours, gate on p99 latency, OOMs, and jemalloc arena growth. If any threshold hit, auto rollback.
Oliver: I'll wire up the alert rules. Proposed prometheus queries: `sum(rate(process_resident_memory_bytes[5m])) by (service)` and `rate(jemalloc_fragmentation_ratio[5m])` — want p95 and p99 over window.
Maria: Also capture allocation churn: `increase(jemalloc_allocs_total[10m])` and `je_prof stack samples` if we can. Plus CPU steal spikes.
Jin: I'll deploy canary with 3 hosts, configure autoscale to not kick in (we want to see natural behavior), and run the 2h soak with the production load generator. Planning start at 17:00 UTC.
Samir: Make sure deploy records an audit-log entry for the package bump (who/sha). We need the KMS key usage logged too (deploy’s image signing). deploy-bot, can you add the audit note?
deploy-bot: audit: package bump jemalloc@6.2.1 by jin@redwood, commit sha abcdef1234, ksign_key=kms-prod-3, entry_id=audit-20260303-01
Oliver: Nice. I'll create temporary alert policies:
- p99 latency > baseline + 30ms over 5m -> rollback
- jemalloc_fragmentation_ratio > 1.15 for 10m -> rollback
- process_resident_memory_bytes growth > 200MB in 15m -> rollback
- OOM/killed -> immediate rollback
Maria: Add perf regression check: run the internal perf harness (100 concurrent sessions) before and after canary and diff tail latencies. If >10% regression at p99 we halt.
Jin: Running harness now against staging patched binary; will post results. If all green, start canary at 17:00 UTC.
Samir: thanks all. After canary, we'll keep canary tags and a 24h monitoring window before full rollout. Also log this thread in the vuln triage board with post-patch results.
Jin: quick update (16:42) — perf harness p99 baseline 180ms -> patched 190ms (+5.5%). CPU and allocs slightly higher but within thresholds. Proceeding to canary at 17:00 UTC.
Oliver: I'll stand by the alert channel and be ready to flip rollback.
Maria: I'll own the post-canary report.
Samir: Great — please paste the perf diffs and jemalloc profiles into the vuln board thread after the run. :thumbsup:
